title: Gaussian generator from Hermite coefficients
statement: Let $n\ge0$, and let $f,g\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure. Suppose that for every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of $g$ at $\alpha$ equals $|\alpha|$ times the Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$, where $|\alpha|=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i$. Then $f$ has Gaussian generator $g$: both functions are square-integrable, and as $t\to0^+$, the $L^2$ norm under product standard Gaussian measure of $(f-P_{e^{-t}}f)/t-g$ tends to zero, where $P_\rho f(x)=\mathbb E[f(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)]$ and $Y$ has product standard Gaussian law.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is in $L^2$ of product standard Gaussian measure
